conventions.convention: Finite-volume data are averages over I_i=[ih,(i+1)h), centered at (i+1/2)h; the right face x_{i+1/2} is (i+1)h. Superscripts − and + denote traces from the left and right cells.
Nodal ENO2 uses separate point samples at y_j=jh, selects between two quadratic interpolants by absolute second divided differences, and resolves ties to the left.
WENO ideal weights are (1/10,6/10,3/10). The default epsilon is positive and independent of h; the WENO-Z comparison uses power p=2.

The MUSCL update is direct reconstructed-upwind forward Euler with no time predictor. Its TVD theorem concerns scalar linear advection, finite-variation bi-infinite data or periodic data, and the inclusive bound |a|Δt/h≤2/3.
The linear monotonicity barrier fixes a noninteger Courant number and finite-stencil coefficients independent of h; second-order consistency matches translation moments through quadratic data.

The Burgers convergence claim applies to the first-order two-point baseline, with h_m=1/m and τ_m=h_m/2, under Countable Choice. Its nonintegrable bounded-BV datum uses the supplier's branch without Dependent Choice.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the minmod MUSCL face states, the separate nodal ENO2 selector, the cell-average WENO5 candidates and JS/Z weights, reflected right states, and the direct reconstructed-upwind forward-Euler update.

For C5 cell-average data, each candidate reproduces polynomials through degree two and has error at most 15 sup|u'''| h³. The ideal combination p_0/10+3p_1/5+3p_2/10 reproduces polynomials through degree four and has error at most (23/15)(3⁵/5!) sup|u⁽⁵⁾| h⁵.

For C5 data on the five-cell stencil, finite stated derivative bounds, and fixed epsilon_0>0 independent of h, both cell-average WENO-JS and WENO-Z face errors are bounded by Ch⁵ for sufficiently small h; the same holds for reflected right states.

The specified direct scalar linear-advection MUSCL/minmod update is TVD for 0≤|a|Δt/h≤2/3 on finite-variation bi-infinite data and N-periodic data for N≥1. For every 2/3<|a|Δt/h≤1, finite-support data of variation 2 have updated variation 3|a|Δt/h; the periodized witness works for every N≥7.
For C2 data with |u'|≥c>0 on the cell neighborhood, both MUSCL/minmod face errors are bounded by Ch² for sufficiently small h, where C depends only on c and a bound for |u''|.

published_dependencies.used_for: Uniqueness identifies the selected Newton quadratic with the three-node polynomial interpolant in the ENO2 proof.
The three-node remainder formula gives the ENO2 bound Mh³/16 for either candidate stencil.
Taylor remainder bounds establish the MUSCL face estimate and the candidate and ideal WENO reconstruction estimates.
The Burgers example checks all scalar Kruzhkov entropy jump inequalities and the strong local L1 initial trace.
Identifies the Countable Choice assumption carried by the Burgers example's imported monotone finite-volume convergence theorem.

concerns.concern: The prose says, “The final counterexample computes the new extrema produced by unlimited centered slopes.” That counterexample is the second listed item; the final listed item is the Burgers example. The positional description does not match the page inventory.

seams_checked.note: The actual use is in the Burgers companion example. It checks bounded translation variation, the nonintegrable-data Countable Choice branch, a globally defined locally Lipschitz flux monotone on [0,1]², the full CFL bound, and the positive time-to-space ratio. Convergence is asserted for the first-order baseline, without extending it to subsequent MUSCL updates.

The Burgers example uses the Rankine–Hugoniot identity at states 1 and 0 to obtain speed 1/2 and checks entropy admissibility directly. It does not invoke the supplier page's local systems solver for arbitrary large data or infer system TVD from characteristic reconstruction.

The consumer's Prerequisite interface explicitly makes this a page-reading prerequisite and states that its proofs invoke no MUSCL, ENO, WENO, TVD, or fully discrete time-stepping result. Its first-order HLL and semidiscrete entropy claims do not overstate this batch's scalar reconstruction results.
